data.gender_notes: Millard is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old English words 'mylge' (mildew) and 'heard' (brave, hardy). The name Millard originated as a nickname for a brave and hardy soldier or ruler. The name Millard carries the meaning “Soldier, ruler” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Millard usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing courage and strength.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Millard total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

Millards have been known throughout history for their courage and resilience. In modern times, the name has been given to boys with a strong sense of character and a desire to be leaders and protectors.

Ultimately, the spiritual significance of the name Millard lies in its ability to inspire and motivate individuals to be brave, resilient, and committed to their beliefs and values.
